Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Energy Corp. Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. [Operator Instructions] Please note this event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Energy Corp.'s Third Quarter 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Maria Gonzalez, Chief Financial Officer; Robert Kline, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Elena Vasquez, VP of Exploration.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we make today may be forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Apex Energy Corp. delivered solid results in the third quarter, driven by strong operational performance and favorable commodity prices. We achieved record production volumes averaging 255,000 barrels of oil equivalent per day, up 12% year-over-year. I'm particularly pleased with our progress in the midstream segment, where transportation volumes hit new highs, and our ongoing infrastructure expansions are locking in long-term cash flows. We're focused on advancing our exploration and drilling program, highlighted by standout well results in the Permian and Eagle Ford. Further, our refining operations posted robust throughput and margins amid resilient crack spreads. Finally, we're guiding capital expenditures thoughtfully to ensure high returns while advancing environmental initiatives that reduced spills significantly.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Maria Gonzalez to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Maria Gonzalez: Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Our revenue was $6.8 billion, up 22% year-over-year. Operating income was $1.45 billion, and net income was $1.1 billion. We generated $1.5 billion in free cash flow and returned $750 million to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. Our balance sheet remains strong, with $10.2 billion in debt and $3.1 billion in cash.

To provide more color on our segment performance, let me start with midstream, which continues to be the bedrock of our business model, contributing over 85% of our adjusted EBITDA through long-term, fee-based contracts with investment-grade producers and a diversified portfolio across crude oil, natural gas, and NGLs. Transportation volumes were a standout this quarter, with overall throughput across our system reaching a record 2.8 million boe/d, up 12% year-over-year and 4% sequentially. Breaking it down: crude oil volumes averaged 1.6 million bpd, a 15% YoY increase driven by Permian Basin production surges, with our Delaware Basin gathering systems, including the 550-mile Apex Crude Header pipeline, exceeding 95% utilization at average tariffs of $1.85 per barrel. This ties to Permian rig counts at 310 active rigs and tightening WTI differentials to $1.20/bbl below NYMEX.

Natural gas transportation hit 4.2 Bcf/d, up 9% YoY, supported by Haynesville and Appalachian ramps, with firm revenues up 11% to $285 million from our 1.2 Bcf/d capacity on the Apex Connector Pipeline to Gulf Coast LNG facilities. Henry Hub averaged $2.75/MMBtu, and our take-or-pay contracts now cover 92% of gas volumes. NGL volumes were 650,000 bpd, up 6% sequentially, with our Eagle Ford fractionation complex at 85% capacity generating $120 million in fees.

These results drove midstream EBITDA to $525 million, up 14% YoY with 72% margins, and utilization-adjusted EBITDA per flowing boe at $2.45, up 8%, aided by operational discipline and lower Texas ad valorem taxes. On infrastructure, we've deployed $650 million YTD of our $2.1 billion 2023-2025 program. Key wins include the 400 MMcf/d Phase II Waha Hub Connector online ahead of schedule, adding $45 million annual EBITDA; the $450 million Apex Permian Link crude pipeline advancing to Q4 2024 completion with SCADA and drone leak detection; a $300 million JV for 800 MMcf/d Golden Pass Connector capacity with binding 12-year ship-or-pay deals; and the $150 million Eagle Ford NGL Loop with energy-saving upgrades.

The Permian drives 55% of volumes, Haynesville gas up 18% YoY, offsetting Bakken softness, while Appalachia storage yielded $25 million in optimization. We're embedding ESG, with electrification cutting Scope 1 emissions 30% and CCUS pilots targeting 2 MMtpa by 2026. We reaffirm FY24 midstream EBITDA of $2.1-2.2 billion, backed by a $4.5 billion project backlog at 12-15% IRRs and 70% FCF conversion, hedged against Waha weakness.

Turning to refining, which contributed over 40% of adjusted EBITDA, we processed record volumes at 1.28 million bpd, up 8% quarter-over-quarter and 12% YoY, at 92% utilization of our 1.4 million bpd capacity. Our Port Arthur Gulf Coast complex averaged 850,000 bpd post-turnaround, Midwest Joliet at 380,000 bpd, and Rotterdam JV at 250,000 bpd. Q4 throughput guides to 1.25-1.30 million bpd, idling lower-complexity units.

Margins held firm with system-wide GRM at $18.20/bbl, up 22% YoY on 3:2:1 cracks of $24.50/bbl, gasoline at $28/bbl, distillate $26/bbl. Yields optimized to 48% gasoline, 26% ULSD, with $2.50/bbl from Group 3 base oils. Gulf Coast led at $20.10/bbl on exports, Midwest $16.80/bbl with RINs, Rotterdam $15.40/bbl. Hedging 60% Q4 cracks at $22/bbl floors.

Efficiency shone with costs at $4.65/bbl, down 14% YoY, energy intensity at 85,000 BTU/bbl via AI flare recovery and digital twins boosting yields 102.5%. Renewables ramped with Joliet's 20,000 bpd unit generating $250 million annualized RINs. Refining EBITDA hit $850 million, ROIC 22%, full-year guide $3.2-3.5 billion.

Finally, on capital expenditure guidance, we're steering total 2025 capex to $5.8-6.4 billion, up 5-10% from 2024's $5.5 billion, assuming $75-85 Brent and $2.75-3.50 Henry Hub. Upstream 55-60% or $3.3-3.8 billion on PUDs; exploration 15-20% or $1.0-1.3 billion; midstream 10-15% or $700-950 million; low-carbon 10% or $600-700 million for CCUS and electrification targeting 25% emissions cut by 2030.

Permian gets $2.8-3.2 billion with 28 rigs; Gulf of Mexico $1.2-1.5 billion on Winterfell and Lobster; North Sea $400 million; Guyana $600 million for Liza South; UAE JV $300 million. Tech like AI simulation boosts EURs 8%, Olympus CCUS at 15-20% IRR. Portfolio 85% above 15% IRR hurdle, $12 billion NPV10, generating $2.5 billion FCF for deleveraging to 1.0x, 4.2% dividend, $1.5 billion buybacks. Flexible to toggle 15-20% on macros.

I will now turn the call over to Robert Kline for an operational update.

Robert Kline: Thank you, Maria. On the operational front, we continue to execute our strategy effectively. Our production averaged 255,000 boe/d. We successfully brought the Apex State 101H and other key wells online, which are expected to contribute significantly to our production growth.

Now, turning to our exploration and drilling activities, we've executed with discipline amid WTI around $75-80/bbl, focusing on Tier 1 Permian inventory with extensions to Eagle Ford and DJ Basin. Our high-graded 1.2 million net acre position shows sub-$40 breakevens and 98% drilling success YTD.

Key Q3 results: Permian Delaware Basin's 12 Second Bone Spring wells, led by Apex State 101H's 12,500-foot lateral IP30 of 1,850 boe/d (82% oil), 15% above type curve, 1.4 MMboe EUR at $7.2 million D&C, down 12%. Program IP30 averaged 1,620 boe/d on 11,800-foot laterals, fiber optics cutting interference 20%. Eagle Ford's Hawk 15H pad IP30 1,120 boe/d (75% oil), costs $5.8 million, flaring 0.5%. Guyana Liza South-2 appraisal shows 250 feet net pay.

Drilling: 28 gross spuds, 18 days to spud, 22-day cycles with AI geosteering cutting NPT 30%. 2025 D&C $1.8 billion: 70% Permian (150 locations post-Oxy bolt-on), 12-14 rigs, 15,000-foot laterals. DJ farm-down de-risks Niobrara. F&D $8.50/boe, 220% replacement, PDP to 95,000 boe/d.

Now I'll turn it over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for an update on our exploration activities.

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Thank you, Robert. Building on the COO's updates, we're excited about the potential of our exploration program. We recently completed a successful seismic survey in the Permian Basin and are planning to drill 28 exploration wells next year, with high-impact potential to add significant reserves through wildcats and appraisals like Guyana and Keathley Canyon.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from Sarah Jenkins with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thanks, and good morning, team. Could you walk us through the environmental performance section from the Q3 deck, specifically spills, incidents, and remediation efforts? How are those trending, and any color on regional variances or new initiatives?

Maria Gonzalez: Good morning, Sarah. Happy to dive in. At Apex Energy, environmental stewardship is a core pillar of our ESG framework, and Q3 capped our strongest year yet on spills and incidents, with a 47% YoY reduction in reportable spill volume to 142 barrels from 267 in 2023, below our under-200 barrel target and better than peers like ExxonMobil's 180-barrel upstream average.

By metrics under API RP 75 and SPCC plans: zero Tier 1 spills (first since Macondo tightened BSEE regs), Tier 2 down to 5 from 9 (pipeline-related), Tier 3 steady at 12 (frac overflows). MTBSE up to 28,000 hours from 19,500 via $150 million in digital twins and analytics.

Permian (55% production) cut spills 60% to 65 barrels with DAS on 1,200 miles of lines, 92% water recycling. Gulf of Mexico (18 platforms) 42 barrels Tier 3, 100% SEMS II compliance post-Ida. North Sea zero spills under OSPAR.

Remediation closed 98% sites in 90 days at $28.4 million (0.3% capex): bioremediation in Eagle Ford to <100 ppm TPH, Corexit for GoM sheen, drone LiDAR cutting response 40%. ERM audits show 95% habitat recovery per EPA protocols.

We're shifting to zero-harm with $200 million 2025 capex for SLB Delfi AI leak detection, targeting 25% MTBSE uplift, boosting ESG score to 78/100. Saves $50 million yearly in fines/downtime, aids green bonds at 45 bps over Treasuries. Operator, back to you.

Operator: Our next question comes from Mike Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson: Good morning. What are your expectations for refining margins and throughput into next year?

Maria Gonzalez: Good morning, Mike. As detailed earlier, we're positioned well with hedged cracks and high utilization. Expect Q4 GRMs around $18-20/bbl on steady demand, full-year refining EBITDA $3.2-3.5 billion, focusing on yield optimization and renewables for sustained 22% ROIC amid $20-22 crack forecasts.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Could you please provide more color on drilling cycle times and cost reductions in the Permian?

Robert Kline: Good morning, Lisa. We've hit record lows at 22 days spud-to-release using Super Spec rigs drilling 1.2 miles/day, AI geosteering in the zone 95% of time, cutting NPT 30% and D&C 12% to $7.2 million, extending to longer laterals for top-decile returns.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Patel with BMO Capital. Please go ahead.

David Patel: How will the results of the exploration program affect the company's future strategy?

Dr. Elena Vasquez: Good morning, David. These strong results, like 220% reserve replacement and sub-$40 breakevens, reinforce our multi-basin focus, extending inventory to 5+ years, prioritizing Permian and Guyana for 10% PDP growth and $1.2 billion 2025 FCF, while de-risking new ventures flexibly.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I would like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Hale for closing remarks.

Johnathan Hale: Thank you, Operator. In summary, we are pleased with our performance in Q3 2024. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
